final_answer:
**Answer: two high-criticality pFMEA risks have OQ coverage but no PQ coverage where PQ would be expected: FM-02 and FM-13.** Both are in RA-PFMEA-001 and both have an RPN of 120.

**How I traced coverage:** Risks link to requirements through MITIGATES/ASSESSES links. Requirements (and the CS/FS/DS items that trace to them) link to test cases through VERIFIES links. Each test case belongs to an OQ or PQ protocol. I treated a risk as "OQ-covered" or "PQ-covered" if any of its mitigating requirements was verified by a test in an OQ or PQ protocol.

**How I defined "PQ expected":** No document in the database states this explicitly, so this is my inference. I applied it to requirements whose wording is about performance under representative or loaded conditions, since those are what PQ normally demonstrates. Alarm, control, data, and security requirements were not counted as PQ-expected.

**The two risks:**
- **FM-02 (wrong or edited selection program run; CD3 purity, CD4/CD8 ratio).** Mitigated by URS-PRDG-002, which requires locked, version-controlled parameters and CD3+ purity of at least 90%. TC-OQ-PRDG-02 (OQ-PRDG-01) verifies only the program lock and version check. No PQ test covers purity. PQ-PRDG-01 covers only closed processing (URS-PRDG-001).
- **FM-13 (deviation from the programmed freeze curve; post-thaw viability).** Mitigated by URS-CRF-001, which requires CRF-P01 to run within ±2 °C of the curve "with a representative load." TC-OQ-CRF-01 was executed on an empty chamber. OQ-CRF-01 is the only protocol for SYS-CRF, and there is no PQ protocol for the controlled-rate freezer.

**Risks I excluded:**
- FM-09, FM-07 and FM-03 have PQ coverage on their performance requirements (URS-INC-001, URS-ULT-001, URS-PRDG-001).
- FM-16 (door left open) depends on the door-open alarm, which is an alarm requirement. Its only OQ test (TC-OQ-INC-04) failed on INC-03 (DEV-26-011, closed under an exception). That gap is an OQ issue rather than a PQ-expected gap, so I left it out.
- FM-05, FM-06, FM-14 and FM-15 map to control or data requirements, not performance requirements.

**Adjacent finding (not a pFMEA item):** The functional risk assessments (val_risk_item rows with FRA IDs) show the same two gaps. FRA-014 (URS-PRDG-002, HIGH) and FRA-020 (URS-CRF-001, HIGH) are OQ-covered with no PQ. I did not include them in the answer because the question asks about FMEA risks.

**Answer: two high-criticality pFMEA risks have OQ coverage but no PQ coverage where PQ would be expected: FM-02 and FM-13.** Both are in RA-PFMEA-001 and both have an RPN of 120.

**How I traced coverage:** Risks link to requirements through MITIGATES/ASSESSES links. Requirements (and the CS/FS/DS items that trace to them) link to test cases through VERIFIES links. Each test case belongs to an OQ or PQ protocol. I treated a risk as "OQ-covered" or "PQ-covered" if any of its mitigating requirements was verified by a test in an OQ or PQ protocol.

**How I defined "PQ expected":** No document in the database states this explicitly, so this is my inference. I applied it to requirements whose wording is about performance under representative or loaded conditions, since those are what PQ normally demonstrates. Alarm, control, data, and security requirements were not counted as PQ-expected.

**The two risks:**
- **FM-02 (wrong or edited selection program run; CD3 purity, CD4/CD8 ratio).** Mitigated by URS-PRDG-002, which requires locked, version-controlled parameters and CD3+ purity of at least 90%. TC-OQ-PRDG-02 (OQ-PRDG-01) verifies only the program lock and version check. No PQ test covers purity. PQ-PRDG-01 covers only closed processing (URS-PRDG-001).
- **FM-13 (deviation from the programmed freeze curve; post-thaw viability).** Mitigated by URS-CRF-001, which requires CRF-P01 to run within ±2 °C of the curve "with a representative load." TC-OQ-CRF-01 was executed on an empty chamber. OQ-CRF-01 is the only protocol for SYS-CRF, and there is no PQ protocol for the controlled-rate freezer.

**Risks I excluded:**
- FM-09, FM-07 and FM-03 have PQ coverage on their performance requirements (URS-INC-001, URS-ULT-001, URS-PRDG-001).
- FM-16 (door left open) depends on the door-open alarm, which is an alarm requirement. Its only OQ test (TC-OQ-INC-04) failed on INC-03 (DEV-26-011, closed under an exception). That gap is an OQ issue rather than a PQ-expected gap, so I left it out.
- FM-05, FM-06, FM-14 and FM-15 map to control or data requirements, not performance requirements.

**Adjacent finding (not a pFMEA item):** The functional risk assessments (val_risk_item rows with FRA IDs) show the same two gaps. FRA-014 (URS-PRDG-002, HIGH) and FRA-020 (URS-CRF-001, HIGH) are OQ-covered with no PQ. I did not include them in the answer because the question asks about FMEA risks.
